title.value: Versatile Energy-Based Models for High Energy Physics
title.justification: The paper explores the use of energy-based models to simulate interactions in high energy physics, specifically at the Large Hadron Collider.
title.quote: We build a versatile energy-based model for High Energy Physics events at the Large Hadron Collider.

extractions.description: The paper discusses the development and application of Energy-Based Models (EBMs) for high energy physics events at the Large Hadron Collider. It presents a generative framework for modeling particle interactions using EBMs, highlighting their flexibility and use in tasks like parameterized event generation, anomaly detection, and classification. A focus is on leveraging the self-attention mechanism to model complex inter-particle interactions, with applications in background estimation and signal detection. The paper also addresses improvements in training EBMs with techniques like the Kullback–Leibler divergence correction.
